discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computing and quantum simulation with controlled atoms: the trapped-ion quantum computer and the optical-lattice Hubbard-model quantum simulator

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

subfield: Quantum optics / atomic physics / quantum information
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed how isolated atoms can be turned into programmable quantum matter. Their 1995 proposal of a trapped-ion quantum computer set out the first realistic architecture for universal quantum logic. It led directly to entangling gates in ion traps, and today's ion-based processors still follow that design. In 1998, with Jaksch, Bruder and Gardiner, they showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model and predicted a superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition. Experiments soon confirmed it, and it became the foundation of analogue quantum simulation. Their later work on quantum repeaters, quantum networks, synthetic gauge fields and tensor-network methods shaped how the field understands entanglement in many-body systems. Few theoretical ideas have moved so directly into decisive experiments across so many laboratories. Their proposals founded a new discipline linking atomic physics, condensed matter and quantum information.
